# SHOPSMART AI

Solution design

## 1. PROBLEM AND SOLUTION OVERVIEW

Customers struggle to find suitable products, compare options, understand shopping policies, and obtain order information. ShopSmart AI provides a responsive shopping interface and one AI assistant that uses catalog data, approved knowledge documents, and customer order information. The application demonstrates the case-study requirements using sample data, approved sample documents, simulated orders, and mocked delivery events.

### Committed scope

| Area | Implementation commitment |
| --- | --- |
| Shopping | Login, catalog, category hierarchy, search, category/brand/price filters, price/rating sorting, pagination, comparison, wishlist, cart, preferences, and responsive layout. |
| Recommendations | Interpret intent, extract requirements, apply product constraints, recommend catalog matches, explain reasons, check availability, and clarify incomplete requests. |
| Knowledge assistant | Upload PDF, Markdown, and JSON; extract, chunk, embed, retrieve, and generate grounded answers with document references. |
| Order tracking | Retrieve simulated customer orders and mocked shipment events. |
| Agent coordination | One assistant calls backend services for product search, inventory, order status, and knowledge retrieval. |
| Explainability and audit | Display reasons and citations; record requests, tool activity, source references, outcomes, and timestamps. |

### Scope boundaries

- No payment integration.
- No real carrier or external marketplace integrations.
- No stock forecasting, promotion management, or pricing automation.
- No production-scale deployment in the initial implementation.
- Cancellation eligibility is informational; the assistant does not execute cancellations.

## 2. ASSUMPTIONS AND USER JOURNEYS

### Implementation assumptions

- Seeded demo accounts represent existing customer authentication and identify Basic, Prime, or Premium membership.
- Sample products include the required product fields and specifications for comparison.
- Inventory is centrally managed; an internal warehouse API supplies seeded warehouse data.
- Orders are simulated and delivery events are mocked.
- Approved knowledge documents include version, effective date, category, and region.
- Chat and embedding models are accessible during development.

### Required user journeys

| Journey | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Login | Sign in; view membership and preferences. |
| Browse and find | Navigate categories; search; filter by category, brand and price; sort by price or rating; paginate. |
| Compare | View selected products and specifications side by side. |
| Wishlist | Add and remove products. |
| Cart | Add products, change quantities, remove items, display total. |
| Preferences | Save preferred categories, brands, and budget. |
| Recommendations | Return matching catalog products with supported reasons and availability; ask clarifying questions. |
| Policy question | Answer from approved documents with document, section and version references. |
| Knowledge upload | Upload PDF, Markdown, or JSON with required metadata. |
| Order tracking | Retrieve the customer’s simulated order and shipment events. |
| Combined assistance | Coordinate product, inventory, order and policy lookups. |

The interface adapts to desktop and mobile screen sizes. Membership is part of the customer profile; no additional benefits are assumed.

## 3. ARCHITECTURE AND RESPONSIBILITIES

**Architecture:** React + Vite UI → Spring Boot API → Shopping services / Spring AI + tools / Document ingestion + RAG → PostgreSQL + pgvector and chat/embedding models

The backend is one application with separate shopping, AI, knowledge, orders, and security packages, keeping local execution manageable.

| Component | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| React UI | Shopping screens, chat, document upload, order display, and source references. |
| Spring Boot API | Authentication, input validation, responses, and coordination. |
| Shopping services | Catalog, categories, comparison, wishlist, cart, and preferences. |
| Spring AI assistant | Interpret intent, call backend tools, and generate structured responses. |
| Backend tools | Read product, warehouse inventory, order, and shipment information. |
| RAG service | Parse, chunk, embed, retrieve evidence, and answer document questions. |
| PostgreSQL / pgvector | Shopping data, knowledge documents/chunks, audit records, and vector search. |
| Model provider | Chat generation and embeddings. |

## 5. API CONTRACTS

All APIs use JSON except multipart document upload. Protected endpoints use the authenticated customer identity. Only APIs required for the committed case-study functionality are included.

| Method and endpoint | Request | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST /api/auth/login | Email, password | Session and customer profile |
| GET /api/categories | None | Category hierarchy |
| GET /api/products | Search, category, brand, price range, sort, page, size | Products and pagination |
| GET /api/products/{id} | Product ID | Details, specifications, availability |
| GET /api/products/compare | Product IDs | Comparison details |
| GET /api/preferences | None | Customer preferences |
| PUT /api/preferences | Categories, brands, budget | Saved preferences |
| GET /api/wishlist | None | Wishlist products |
| POST /api/wishlist | Product ID | Updated wishlist |
| DELETE /api/wishlist/{productId} | Product ID | Updated wishlist |
| GET /api/cart | None | Items and total |
| POST /api/cart/items | Product ID, quantity | Updated cart |
| PUT /api/cart/items/{productId} | Quantity | Updated cart |
| DELETE /api/cart/items/{productId} | Product ID | Updated cart |
| GET /api/orders | None | Customer orders |
| GET /api/orders/{id} | Order ID | Order and shipment events |
| GET /api/inventory/{productId} | Product ID | Warehouse quantities and availability |
| POST /api/documents | File, version, effective date, category, region | Document ID and ingestion status |
| POST /api/ai/recommendations | Message | Recommendation response |
| POST /api/ai/knowledge | Question, category/region context | Knowledge response |
| POST /api/ai/chat | Message | Response from coordinated shopping, order, or knowledge tools |

## 6. RESPONSE FORMATS AND AI WORKFLOWS

### Recommendation response – source contract

```json
{
  "interpretedRequirement": "Laptop for Java development and AI learning",
  "budget": 1000,
  "recommendations": [
    {
      "productId": "LAP101",
      "productName": "Dell Inspiron 15",
      "reason": "16GB RAM, Intel i7 processor, SSD storage",
      "availability": "IN_STOCK"
    }
  ],
  "clarifyingQuestion": null
}
```

### Recommendation workflow

1. Read the message and saved preferences.
2. Extract category, budget, use, and specifications. Ask a question if essential details are missing.
3. Search catalog products with the required filters.
4. Check inventory and explain recommendations using actual product specifications.
5. Validate and return the structured response.

Recommendations must refer to real catalog products and respect budget constraints.

### Knowledge response – source contract

```json
{
  "answer": "Opened laptops can be returned within 7 days if physical damage is not present.",
  "confidence": "HIGH",
  "sources": [
    {
      "document": "Laptop Return Policy",
      "section": "Opened Products",
      "version": "2026.1"
    }
  ],
  "followUpRequired": false
}
```

The policy above is illustrative and may be returned only when supported by an uploaded, approved document.

### Common error response

```json
{
  "code": "INVALID_REQUEST",
  "message": "Quantity must be greater than zero."
}
```

## 7. KNOWLEDGE, COORDINATION, AND SAFEGUARDS

### How the knowledge assistant works

Upload an approved PDF, Markdown, or JSON file. The backend reads the text, splits it into small chunks, creates embeddings, and stores them with document metadata. When a customer asks a question, it finds relevant chunks and answers using only that evidence. The response cites the document, section, and version. If evidence is missing or contradictory, it says so and asks for clarification. Confidence means strength of supporting evidence: HIGH = direct support, MEDIUM = partial support, LOW = insufficient or conflicting evidence. It is not a statistical probability.

### How the assistant coordinates services

For a request such as “Where is my order, and can I cancel after shipment?”, the assistant checks the customer’s order status, retrieves the applicable cancellation policy, and combines the results with citations. It explains eligibility but does not cancel the order.

### Basic safeguards

- Use authenticated customer identity for orders, cart, wishlist, and preferences; do not expose another customer’s data.
- Store hashed passwords and keep model keys in backend environment variables.
- Only the configured demo uploader can upload documents; only approved documents are used in answers.
- Validate all API inputs and tool arguments; document text is evidence, not an instruction source.
- Show simple error messages for missing products, unavailable stock, bad files, insufficient evidence, and model timeouts.
- Keep normal shopping features usable if AI is unavailable. Save request, tools, sources, outcome, and timestamp in audit records.

## 8. STAGE-WISE IMPLEMENTATION ROADMAP

The first four stages produce a complete working demonstration of the base ShopSmart AI case-study requirements. Stages five and six are optional, open-ended directions for later improvements—not commitments for the initial demo.

| Stage | Implementation focus | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stage 1 – Foundation and catalog | Set up React/Vite, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL/pgvector, schema, seed data, authentication, and membership profiles. Implement categories, product listings, search, filters, sorting, pagination, comparison, and responsive UI. | Working catalog and authenticated shopping UI. |
| Stage 2 – Shopping and order tracking | Implement preferences, wishlist, cart, quantity updates, totals, warehouse inventory, simulated orders, and shipment event display. Apply ownership checks and input validation. | Working end-to-end basic shopping and order lookup. |
| Stage 3 – AI product discovery | Connect chat model and Spring AI tools. Interpret shopping requests, extract budget/specifications, search the existing catalog, verify stock, return reasons and clarifying questions. | Working AI product recommendation demo. |
| Stage 4 – RAG and integrated assistant | Upload PDF/Markdown/JSON, chunk, embed, retrieve only approved content, display grounded citations, coordinate order + policy queries, and record audits. Test error handling and integrated UI. | Complete functional demo of all basic case-study requirements. |
| Stage 5 – Future enhancements (open-ended) | Potential directions: better product ranking, richer customer personalization, improved document quality checks, observability and automated testing. Scope chosen after Stage 4. | Optional improvements; not part of the base demo. |
| Stage 6 – Production scalability (open-ended) | Potential directions: cloud deployment, monitoring, caching, queues for ingestion, scalable vector search, stronger identity controls, and resilience. Assess load and cost before selecting architecture. | Optional production-readiness roadmap. |

Scope note: payment processing, live carrier integration, stock forecasting, promotions, and automated order cancellation are not included in the four-stage base demo.
